# Source Tree Analysis

*Generated by the BMad document-project workflow — deep scan, 2026-07-17.*

## Repository Layout

## Critical Directories

- **`apps/web/app/api/looms/`** — the HTTP surface for the entire loom lifecycle (scope → orchestrate →
  build → verify → repair → ready → accept → done). Every state transition the cockpit UI can trigger is
  a route under here, including the human-only `accept` route — there is no agent-callable accept
  endpoint anywhere in the tree, matching the domain rule in the root README.
- **`packages/core/src/`** — the loom engine proper. `engine.ts`/`tick.ts`/`weave.ts` implement the
  weaver's tick loop; `executor.ts` implements the leaf thread loop; `verifier.ts` and friends implement
  the read-only Verifier. This is the single source of truth for orchestration behavior; `apps/web`
  contains no independent implementation of it, only HTTP/UI plumbing around it.
- **`packages/core/test/`** — a large, flat Bun test suite (98 files) with milestone-prefixed names
  (`m5-`, `m9-`, `m10-`, `m11-`, `b1-`, `b2-`) that track incremental spec milestones directly in the
  filenames, e.g. `m11-runnable-shape.test.ts`, `m10-lane-escalation.test.ts`.
- **`apps/web/lib/`** — everything that isn't a React component or a route handler: MCP bridges
  (`loom-mcp.ts`, `ultra-mcp.ts`), file-backed persistence (`store.ts`), permission gating
  (`permissions.ts`), and the demo-gallery/fixture system used for visual QA.
- **`apps/web/components/looms/`** and **`apps/web/components/session/`** — the two largest,
  most domain-specific component groups; they render loom state (god-view, weave-orgchart, thread-tree,
  verifier-report-card) and live chat/session UI respectively.
- **`apps/desktop/`** — a thin shell: it contains no application logic of its own, only the Electron
  boot process (`main.js`), a build script that assembles a Next.js standalone bundle
  (`build-app.sh`), and electron-builder packaging config.
- **`scripts/e2e/greenfield-next/`** — the project's own scripted end-to-end scenario, exercising a
  "greenfield Next.js project" through Telar's loom lifecycle from the outside.

## Entry Points

| Entry point | Path | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Web app router root layout | `apps/web/app/layout.tsx` | Wraps every page with fonts, `ThemeProvider`, `DockProvider`, `AppSidebar`; injects a pre-paint theme-init script |
| Web server boot hook | `apps/web/instrumentation.ts` | Next's `register()` — dynamically imports `@telar/core` (Node-runtime-guarded) and runs `reconcileStuckLooms()` on every server boot |
| Desktop shell | `apps/desktop/main.js` | Forks the standalone Next server as a child process, points a `BrowserWindow` at it; supports `TELAR_DESKTOP_URL` override and `--smoke` boot-check mode |
| Core package barrel | `packages/core/src/index.ts` | `export *` barrel for most core modules (verifier.ts, verify-lane.ts, and runnable-shape.ts are NOT re-exported — internal-only); the sole consumption path for `@telar/core` (no compiled `dist/`, TS source consumed directly) |
| CLI launcher | `scripts/telar` | Bun-shebang script; starts/re-opens the stable cockpit, tracks PID/log/config under `~/.telar/launcher/` |
| Desktop build orchestrator | `scripts/build-desktop.sh` | Builds a distributable `Telar.app` from a pristine git snapshot of an origin ref |

## Integration Points

- **`apps/web` → `packages/core`**: declared as `"@telar/core": "workspace:*"` in
  `apps/web/package.json`, resolved by Bun workspaces to `packages/core` (no build/publish step — the
  package's `exports["."]` points straight at `./src/index.ts`). Consumed from route handlers (e.g. the
  `looms/` API tree) and from `apps/web/instrumentation.ts`, `apps/web/lib/loom-mcp.ts`, and
  `apps/web/lib/ultra-mcp.ts`.
- **`apps/desktop` → `apps/web`**: `apps/desktop/build-app.sh` runs `next build` inside `apps/web` with
  `NEXT_OUTPUT=standalone NEXT_DIST_DIR=.next-desktop`, producing a standalone server tree at
  `apps/web/.next-desktop/standalone/apps/web/server.js`. `apps/desktop/main.js` forks that
  `server.js` as a child process and points its `BrowserWindow` at the resulting local URL. Because
  Next's output tracing misses two runtime dependencies, `build-app.sh` also manually copies in
  `@playwright/mcp` (for the packaged, sandboxed Verifier) and the `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`
  platform-specific native CLI binary.
- **`scripts/build-desktop.sh` → `apps/desktop/build-app.sh`**: the top-level orchestrator (fetch a
  pristine `git worktree` of an origin ref → frozen install → invoke `build-app.sh` → stamp
  `build-info.json` → `electron-builder --dir` → atomic swap into `--out` → smoke-test the result).
  It deliberately never reads the working tree, so uncommitted local changes can never ship.
- **`apps/desktop/package.json` `build.extraResources`**: pulls `apps/web/.next-desktop/standalone`
  (plus its `.bun` node_modules store and the playwright-mcp bundle) into the packaged `.app` via
  electron-builder — the concrete link between the web build output and the desktop package.
  `apps/desktop/package.json` also sets `"trustedDependencies": ["electron"]`.
- **Telar dogfoods itself**: the repo root has its own `telar.yaml` (`name: telar, adapter: plain,
  account: personal, baseBranch: main`, with a `test` gate running `bun test`), meaning Telar's own
  development can be run as a Telar loom against its own codebase.
- **`bunfig.toml` ↔ `apps/desktop`/`apps/web` build outputs**: `[test].pathIgnorePatterns` excludes
  `apps/desktop/release/**` and `apps/web/.next-desktop/**` from `bun test` discovery, because those
  build outputs contain copies of web source (including `*.test.ts` files) that must never run as if
  they were live tests.
- **Root `package.json` workspaces**: `["apps/*", "packages/*"]` is the mechanism by which Bun links
  `web`, `telar-desktop`, and `@telar/core` together and resolves `workspace:*` dependencies.

## File Organization Patterns

- **`apps/web/app`** follows Next.js App Router conventions strictly: every route segment that serves
  HTTP is a `route.ts` file (never a bare handler at the segment root), every dynamic segment uses
  bracket folders (`[id]`, `[name]`, `[...path]` for catch-all evidence/spec file trees), and UI pages
  are `page.tsx` alongside an optional `layout.tsx` (only `demo-gallery/` defines a nested layout). API
  route nesting mirrors resource hierarchy exactly — e.g.
  `app/api/projects/[name]/git/remote/issues/[number]/comment/route.ts` — rather than flattening query
  params into a single handler.
- **`apps/web/components`** is organized by *domain*, not by Next.js routing structure: `looms/`,
  `projects/`, `session/`, `settings/` group components by the feature they render, `ui/` holds
  generic shadcn/base-ui primitives, and `common/` holds cross-domain widgets. This is a deliberate
  split from `app/`, which owns only routing/composition.
- **`apps/web/lib`** mixes server-only helpers (isolated under `lib/server/`) with shared/client-safe
  utilities at the top level; colocated `*.test.ts` files sit next to the module they test
  (`commands.ts` + `commands.test.ts`, `permissions.ts` + `permissions.test.ts`, etc.) rather than in a
  separate `__tests__/` tree.
- **`apps/web/lib/demo-gallery` and `apps/web/lib/gallery-fixtures`** are two related but distinct
  systems: `demo-gallery/` holds the interactive showcase *views* (registry + per-domain entries/lists),
  while `gallery-fixtures/` holds the underlying *scenario data* (`scenarios/app/*.ts`,
  `scenarios/{blocked,charter,chat,...}.ts`) consumed by both the gallery and its own validation test
  (`fixtures.validate.test.ts`).
- **`packages/core/src`** is a flat module directory (no nested feature folders except `runner/`,
  `setup/`, and `ultra/`, each a small, self-contained subsystem) — most cross-cutting concepts
  (loom lifecycle, weaver tick loop, verifier, manifest, MCP, budget) each get exactly one top-level
  `.ts` file, and `index.ts` re-exports most of them as a single flat barrel (verifier.ts,
  verify-lane.ts, and runnable-shape.ts are the exceptions — internal-only, not re-exported). This
  keeps the public API surface (what `apps/web` can import) close to, but not identical to, "everything
  importable from `@telar/core`".
- **`packages/core/test`** is likewise flat and colocated by name with `src/` modules
  (`weave.ts` ↔ `weave.test.ts`, `manifest.ts` ↔ `manifest.test.ts`), but layers on a second naming
  axis — milestone prefixes (`m5-`, `m9-`, `m10-`, `m11-`, `b1-`, `b2-`) — for tests that validate a
  specific spec milestone rather than a single module in isolation.
- **Config-file placement**: each workspace part owns its own `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, and
  (for `web`) `eslint.config.mjs`/`postcss.config.mjs`/`components.json`; only truly repo-wide config
  (`bunfig.toml`, root `package.json`, `telar.yaml` for this repo's own loom runs) lives at the
  repository root.
